title: Guard Your Mind
devotional: Your mind is constantly receiving information, and not everything deserves a permanent place there. Thoughts can come from memories, conversations, entertainment, fears, desires, and the things you repeatedly focus on. Philippians 4:8 gives you a different direction: intentionally think about what is true, honorable, just, pure, lovely, commendable, excellent, and worthy of praise. Guarding your mind does not mean pretending negative thoughts never appear. It means learning what deserves your attention and what you should release.
mind_check: What thought has been taking up too much space in your mind recently?
body_move: When you notice yourself repeatedly feeding an unhealthy thought, change your physical activity. Stand up, walk, exercise, clean, or move into a different environment.
spirit_move: Read Philippians 4:8 slowly. Choose one quality from the verse and intentionally focus your thoughts on something that reflects it.
way_out: When my mind keeps returning to __________, I will redirect my attention toward __________.
prayer: Father, help me guard my mind and become intentional about what I allow to occupy my thoughts. Teach me to recognize thoughts that are pulling me away from You and redirect my attention toward what is true, pure, honorable, and good. Give me discipline over my attention and peace in my mind. Amen.
action: Write down one recurring unhealthy thought. Beside it, write a true and healthy thought you can intentionally focus on when that pattern returns.
